one_liner: Rust/PyO3 io_uring asyncio event loop; claims ~3x lower single-op latency than uvloop, but loses on gather(100).
what_it_does: Replaces the asyncio event loop on Linux. You install it with asyncio.Runner(loop_factory=uringcore.new_event_loop) or the older EventLoopPolicy, and existing asyncio, FastAPI or Starlette code runs unchanged. A Rust core (PyO3 cdylib) owns the io_uring ring, a registered buffer pool, the timers and the ready queue; a Python UringEventLoop (subclass of asyncio.AbstractEventLoop) builds TCP, UDP, Unix sockets, pipes, subprocesses and signals on top of it. Tasks are stock asyncio.Task objects, so debuggers and instrumentation that inspect tasks keep working.
how_it_is_fast: Socket I/O is completion-based: recv, send, accept and connect go to the kernel as io_uring SQEs. It uses multishot recv and a provided-buffer ring on 5.19+, SEND_ZC on 6.0+, registered fixed files and IORING_OP_TIMEOUT timers, and it turns on SQPOLL by default so a kernel thread picks up submissions without io_uring_enter. Completions signal an eventfd registered with the ring, which the Python loop waits on with epoll; the ready queue, timer heap and futures live in Rust to cut per-callback interpreter work, and UDP sendto tries a direct non-blocking syscall first, using the ring only on EAGAIN. The headline single-op wins come from lower per-run_until_complete overhead, not from I/O; each task step still crosses the PyO3 boundary 8-12 times (ARCHITECTURE.md), which is why gather(100) is slower than uvloop.
when_to_use: Linux 5.19+ hosts (6.0+ for SEND_ZC) where you control RLIMIT_MEMLOCK and seccomp, and you want to try io_uring under unmodified asyncio code.

Code that calls run_until_complete() many times on tiny coroutines (CLI tools, test suites, sync-to-async bridges): the committed run shows 3.1-3.6 us per call vs 4.3-5.3 us for stock asyncio and 11-13 us for uvloop.

Plain-TCP or UDP send-heavy services where syscall count or UDP sendto rate matters; the project reports ~831k vs ~550k sendto ops/s over stock asyncio (no hardware given; uvloop does not implement sock_sendto).
Experiments comparing readiness-based and completion-based I/O in Python: the code base is small, Apache-2.0, and ships its benchmark and strace scripts.
when_not_to_use: Fan-out workloads with many concurrent tasks: in the committed run gather(100) takes 188 us vs 116 us for uvloop and 170 us for stock asyncio, and sleep_conc_100 takes 277 us vs 154 us for uvloop.
Timer-heavy code: the committed call_later result is 186 us vs 12.7 us for uvloop; BENCHMARK.md's 13.5 us figure does not appear in any committed output.

TLS servers or clients: create_server, create_connection and create_unix_connection raise NotImplementedError('SSL not yet supported') for ssl=; only start_tls() wraps a transport through a memory BIO, and kTLS is not integrated.

Non-Linux, non-x86-64, or any Python other than 3.13 without a Rust 1.85+ toolchain: PyPI has only 0.9.1 with one cp313 manylinux_2_34 x86_64 wheel, and the 1.0.0 code in the repo (native scheduler, Jan 2026 benchmarks) is not published.
Anything that needs production maturity: one author, 2 stars, no issues ever filed, and the CI Python test steps end in '|| echo ... skipping', so failing tests do not fail the build.

integration.form: module (Python package with a Rust PyO3 cdylib extension, built with maturin)
integration.dependencies: Runtime: typing-extensions. Build: maturin>=1.4 and Rust crates pyo3 0.27, io-uring 0.7, libc, nix 0.30, parking_lot, crossbeam-queue, thiserror, tracing.
integration.min_toolchain: Python 3.10+; Rust 1.85+ (Cargo edition 2024; the README badge 'rust 1.70+' is stale); Linux kernel 5.11+ (5.19+ for multishot recv and provided buffers, 6.0+ for SEND_ZC)
integration.platforms: Linux only. The only published wheel is CPython 3.13 x86_64 manylinux_2_34 (v0.9.1); other targets build from sdist or source.
integration.thread_safety: One loop per thread, as with asyncio; call_soon_threadsafe wakes the loop through the eventfd. Fork is detected by a PID check, and generation IDs invalidate pre-fork buffers. Free-threaded (nogil) Python is untested (listed as future work).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same asyncio loop interface as uvloop (Runner loop_factory or policy), but ssl= on create_server/create_connection raises NotImplementedError, sendfile/sock_sendfile fall through to AbstractEventLoop (NotImplementedError), sock_recv_into/sock_recvfrom_into run in the thread-pool executor, and subprocess and start_tls are beta

gotchas: Each loop mmaps and mlocks its buffer pool with MAP_POPULATE. The code default is 4096 x 8 KiB = 32 MiB per loop; the README says 1024 x 64 KB and the package docstring 512 x 32 KB. A low RLIMIT_MEMLOCK makes loop creation fail with ENOMEM; tune URINGCORE_BUFFER_COUNT and URINGCORE_BUFFER_SIZE.

SQPOLL is on by default (try_sqpoll=True, 1 s idle timeout), so every loop gets a kernel polling thread that spins for up to one second after each submission. The '0 io_uring_enter' strace result moves that cost to a kernel thread; it does not remove it.

The README says 'pure io_uring, no epoll', but the Python loop blocks in select.epoll on the ring's eventfd and uses epoll for add_reader/add_writer. Its poll timeout is capped at 10 ms, so an idle loop wakes about 100 times per second.

The committed benchmark outputs show uringcore failing mid-suite: sock_pair skipped with 'No buffers available for recv' (final_comparison.txt), and the run aborted with "'RuntimeError' object is not callable" (final_report.txt).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over uvloop only on Linux when loop cost is dominated by short run_until_complete calls or uncontended asyncio primitives and you can accept beta TLS and pinned memory; for general servers uvloop is faster on fan-out and timers and far more mature. UCall also drives io_uring from Python but is its own RPC server API rather than an asyncio loop, and monoio or ringline are Rust runtimes that do not run asyncio code.
verified_claims_summary: The 2.9-3.3x figures time one await (sleep(0), an uncontended Lock, an already-resolved Future) inside its own run_until_complete() call; uvloop sits at a flat 11-13 us on every such benchmark, slower than stock asyncio's 4-5 us, so the gap measures loop entry/exit cost, and in the committed run uringcore is only ~1.4x faster than stock asyncio (sleep(0) 3.56 vs 5.25 us) and slower than both on gather(100). The micro-runs used CPython 3.14.2 and Rust release flags (opt-level 3, LTO, 1 codegen unit) on an unnamed 'Linux 6.x' machine; the only hardware stated anywhere is ARCHITECTURE.md's TCP-echo run (AMD Ryzen 7 9700X, WSL2 kernel 6.6.87.2, Python 3.13.3, echo clients as threads in the same process), and VERIFY.md's pinned-CPU run shows parity with uvloop (5,573 vs 5,551 req/s).
status_note: Single-author, Apache-2.0 project whose last commit was 2026-01-11 (quiet for ~8.5 months); PyPI stops at 0.9.1 from 2025-12-28, so using the benchmarked 1.0.0 means building the repo with maturin and Rust 1.85+.
